title: Assessment of the Physical and Environmental Characteristics of NYSC Accommodation Facilities in Oyo State, Nigeria
content: Paramilitary institutions play a critical role in national security, discipline formation, and public order; however, the quality of their residential accommodations significantly influences personnel well-being, performance, and psychological stability. This study assesses paramilitary accommodation facilities in the NYSC orientation camp at Iseyin, Oyo State, with a focus on the available infrastructural components and how functional they are, spatial planning, environmental quality, privacy, safety, and overall habitability. This research sampled 150 corps members purposively and data were collected using a structured questionnaire designed to capture both quantitative and qualitative data. The collected data were analyzed using descriptive statistics such as frequencies and actual counts, supported by charts to visualize infrastructural conditions the corps members were exposed to. The findings concluded that the NYSC camp is equipped with essential infrastructural components, including dormitories, dining halls, toilets, bathrooms, water supply, and electricity, however, high occupancy levels were reported. Physical conditions of the facilities showed functional limitations and maintenance challenges. Movement within dormitories was restricted, issues of poor ventilation, lighting, and sanitation services.
